g.text: Headers stay readable so a peer can sync without the group key. The signature covers the headers
the ciphertext, so a relaying peer cannot re-attribute, re-time or edit an event.

text.tspan: A peer that relays but is not a member
sees the headers, cannot open the payload

g.text: A member holding the group key
Why the signature covers the headers:
re-attributing, re-timing or re-classifying an event changes
, so the signature no longer verifies. Signatures are checked on the way into the log, so one bad event cannot poison a device that later syncs from it.

text.tspan: Readable headers — signed, and used as AEAD associated data
id · UUIDv7, made on the authoring device
author · the device's ed25519 public key, hex
kind · create / edit / delete / sleep_start / sleep_stop
payload — sealed with the baby's group key
verifies — the author id *is* the public key,
so there is no key directory to trust
